author: Copilot
body: `BackendAnalyticsConnectorDto` is defined as `SnakeCased<AnalyticsConnectorDto>`, and `AnalyticsConnectorDto` coerces `startTimestamp` to a `Date`. Because `SnakeCased` preserves `Date` types, `start_timestamp` should be a `Date` here as well; using a string breaks the mock’s TS contract (and can fail typecheck). Prefer `start_timestamp: new Date('...')` (it will serialize to ISO in `HttpResponse.json`) or adjust the backend DTO type so it explicitly models the wire format as a string.

author: mpradhan-nasuni
body: Fixed: start_timestamp now uses Date values (not strings) to match SnakeCased<AnalyticsConnectorDto> type.

author: Copilot
body: `getAnalyticsConnectorDto()` returns a connector with a hard-coded key ending in `...0001`, but `getAnalyticsConnectorKeyDto()` returns `...0002`. With stateless MSW handlers this can lead to inconsistent UI (e.g., after generating a key, a later refetch/refresh can “revert” to the GET key). Consider sharing a single default key constant between both factories (or have `getAnalyticsConnectorKeyDto()` default to `getAnalyticsConnectorDto().key`), and use `overrides` only when a test/scenario needs a different key.

author: Copilot
body: The POST `/cloud_services/analytics_connector` handler returns `getAnalyticsConnectorKeyDto()` (currently a different key than the default GET handler returns via `getAnalyticsConnectorDto()`). Because MSW handlers are stateless, this can create inconsistent behavior if the page refetches after the mutation. Consider returning a key that matches the default GET response (or introducing a scenario/stateful mock for key rotation) so GET/POST stay consistent.

author: mpradhan-nasuni
body: Fixed. POST /cloud_services/analytics_connector now returns the same key as default GET, so the stateless MSW behavior stays consistent across refetches.
